text:
ajordan: Heads up — canary deploy 2026-03-17/ht-merge appears to have a perf regression on p99 for short-chat workloads. CI flagged it but we need to narrow root cause before rollback.
kevin: saw it too. p50 ok, p99 ~2.2x vs baseline. suspect kernel selector change from last merge?
natalie: which merge is the canary pointing at? commit 6f3a2?
ajordan: yep, merge 6f3a2 -> adds kernel-selection heuristics + batching tweak. CI perf suite diff: 
```
baseline p99: 320ms
canary p99: 720ms
delta +400ms (2.25x)
traces show extra kernel splice at step 4 and multiple small kernels instead of fused op
```
ci-bot: CI PERF CHECK FAILED on canary: job perf/smoke-short-chat — regression >= 20% detected. See: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/1799012345
sam: can we reproduce locally? I can run the short-chat harness quickly. instructions?
ajordan: steps: 
1) checkout commit 6f3a2 (the merge)
2) git bisect between parent (stable) and HEAD to narrow to offending commit if needed
3) run ./tools/perf/run_local.sh --profile short-chat --iterations 200 --kv-warm=true --batching=auto
4) compare perf/output/p99.txt with baseline
Command I used: ```git bisect start HEAD 1a2b3c; git bisect run ./tools/perf/ci_bisect_runner.sh```
maria: note: kernel selector config can flip to legacy with env KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy to test if it's selector-related. Also batching heuristic has a new cutoff param BATCH_CUTOFF_MS=5 in the merge.
kevin: good call — try swapping both: KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy BATCH_CUTOFF_MS=8, run harness and post p99.
perf-bot: perf-runner started by sam: run_id=pr-9934 local node gpu0, profiling enabled.
sam: running now, will paste numbers in ~10m.
(10 minutes pass)
sam: first quick run w/ merge defaults: p50 42ms, p95 210ms, p99 730ms. Logs show kernel switch at token 16 where KV cache lookup spikes 1.2ms -> 8.5ms repeatedly.
natalie: KV cache spikes sound like cache warming/regression in recent kv-cache change — does the merge include the new KV eviction tweak?
ajordan: it did. Might be eviction being too aggressive causing misses and repeated loads. But why does kernel selection change too? Maybe the selector uses observed per-token latency to decide kernels causing oscillation.
kevin: hypothesis: batching heuristic cut reduces batch sizes, which changes sequence chunking, exposing a path that triggers kernel splitter. If that increases cold KV misses, p99 rises. Two interacting changes.
maria: can you repro with KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy but merge batching? sam?
sam: run 2 with KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy BATCH_CUTOFF_MS=5 -> p99 335ms (close to baseline). So kernel selector change is major factor.
ajordan: good repro. Next: git bisect inside merge commits to find the exact commit that changed kernel selector behavior. Could be a small refactor.
perf-bot: note: captured perf profile flamegraph at /artifacts/perf/1799012345/flame.svg
kevin: I'll start git bisect today. Quick note: when using git bisect run, the harness must exit non-zero on regression. Use ./tools/perf/check_threshold.sh to compare p99 to baseline.
kevin: starting bisect between parents 1a2b3c (good) and 6f3a2 (bad). Will keep people posted.
(30 minutes)
kevin: bisect narrowed to commit 6f3a2^3 (the third patch in the merge). Diff shows change in kernel_selector: replace heuristic based on avg-token-latency with new moving-median estimator.
natalie: that estimator might be more sensitive to outliers; combined with small batches it may pick wrong kernels. Is there a unit test for selector stability?
maria: not yet. We should add a regression test that runs selector on synthetic traces that mimic KV miss spikes.
ajordan: for immediate mitigation, can we pin KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy in the canary rollout policy or add an automated fallback when p99 > x? We have rollout policy to auto-fallback but it's not triggered for this canary because other metrics looked healthy. We should tweak it.
sam: opened PR to add emergency fallback rule: if p99 > baseline*1.3 for 5m in canary, flip selector to legacy and notify. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/1234
ci-bot: rollback job created: pipeline rollback-canary-1799012345 queued by sam.
kevin: follow-up: I'll revert the selector change in a small revert PR and include test harness. If tests pass and CI perf stable, we can reintroduce the new estimator behind a feature flag and longer canary.
ajordan: thanks all. Action items: kevin bisect + revert PR, sam patch for rollback rule, maria add selector regression unit test, natalie write note in release notes about interaction risk (batching heuristics + selector), perf-bot capture further traces nightly.
maria: ping me if you want help writing the synthetic KV-miss traces. I have a script that simulates LRU churn.
kevin: will update when revert PR is ready.
ajordan: leaving this pinned until rollback completes. :white_check_mark:
